frontmatter.title: Baramulti Suksessarana: a low-calorie coal cash machine at a full price
frontmatter.summary: BSSR sells low-calorie thermal coal into a softening seaborne market. We build a through-cycle NAV off the calibrated realisation and the company's own volume plan, and get a target below the market price: the dividend is real, but so is the state take and the reserve question.
thesis: We initiate at HOLD with a target of Rp4,408, -3.7% versus the Rp5,225 price.

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk (BSSR) at **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of **Rp4,408**, a total return of **-3.7%** against the Rp5,225 price [S0]. BSSR mines thermal coal from two concessions in South and East Kalimantan and sells it almost entirely to export customers, with a large domestic share [S8][S16].

The base case is the most likely path, not a cautious one. We anchor on the last actual year and the company's own plan: FY2025 produced 17.8 Mt and sold 17.6 Mt [S16], and management targets 17.0 Mt for FY2026 [S16]. Our FY2026 volume is 17.0 Mt, so no unexplained decline is assumed. Our realisation is calibrated on the last actual, FY2025 revenue over FY2025 tonnes against that year's Newcastle average [S0], and the model reproduces FY2025 EBITDA of US$102.5m to within a fraction of a percent, so the forecast is built on the last actual's economics rather than on an assumption.

What the market prices and what we think differ on method, not on the company. The multiple and dividend cross-checks value BSSR far above the life-of-asset NAV because they capitalise a near-term, high-payout cash flow; our primary method discounts the same cash flow over the asset's life at through-cycle coal prices. The market appears to be using the dividend-capacity anchor; we are using NAV, and the gap between them is the risk in the name.

The two things that move the value are the coal marker and the royalty. The first is a reviewed deck series: Newcastle averaged US$108/t in the last actual and the desk carries it to US$105/t long run [S0]. The second is the royalty: the licence class is sourced — the operating company mines under a coal contract of work [S19] — but the contract rate is unconfirmed, so it is the single largest unconfirmed input in this initiation. We flag it rather than bury it.

Coal miners are price-takers whose equity is a leveraged call on the marker price and the state take.
In Indonesia the fiscal wedge between the mine gate and the sale is set by the mining licence and the
royalty schedule attached to it, so two otherwise identical pits hand very different shares of the same
tonne to the government. Investors in the sector trade the dividend and the reserve life as much as the
earnings.

BSSR is a thermal-coal producer. It operates through its wholly owned subsidiary PT Antang Gunung Meratus (AGM) in South Kalimantan and through its own blocks in East Kalimantan, and it markets coal to China, India, Japan, Taiwan, the Philippines, Hong Kong, South Korea and Thailand as well as domestically [S8]. The company was incorporated in 1990, is headquartered in Jakarta and is controlled by PT Wahana Sentosa Cemerlang with a very small free float [S0].

The product is a low-calorie thermal coal sold largely to export buyers. In the first half of 2026, export sales were 82.0% of total sales, up from about seven in ten a year earlier [S2]. The FY2025 marketing mix put Indonesia at roughly three-tenths of volume, with China and India the two largest export destinations [S16]. The revenue model is simple and cyclical: tonnes times the realised price, with the realised price a deep discount to the high-grade export marker because the coal is lower in calorific value [S8][S16].

Strategy is price defence and reserve conversion rather than growth. Management deliberately cut output in FY2025, production falling to 17.8 Mt from 21.4 Mt in FY2024 [S16][S9], and said the decision protected margin; the Q1 2026 result was stronger as a consequence [S16]. In parallel the company is drilling to convert its resource base into reserves, running a modest exploration budget on its East Kalimantan blocks in Kutai Kartanegara, and it has said it is looking at new coal assets [S12][S16]. The exploration effort matters more than its size suggests: with proved reserves thin relative to the annual plan rate, the mine's life depends on converting the wider resource base, so drilling results are a first-order input to the value rather than a distant option [S16][S12].

BSSR is a mid-tier producer, not a leader. Its scale is a fraction of the large Indonesian coal names, and its product sits in the lower-grade segment where the buyer set is narrower and the price is more elastic [S8][S10]. It carries no listed subsidiaries beyond its operating company, so the equity is a clean read on one mining business rather than a holding-company puzzle [S8]. The controlling shareholder structure means the shares are effectively a minority claim on a family- and strategically-controlled asset, which shapes both the liquidity and the capital-return decisions [S0].

Indonesian thermal coal is a large, policy-managed export industry. National coal export value rose year on year over the first nine months even as export tonnage fell by roughly thirty million tonnes, because prices rose while volumes dropped [S10]. The government manages supply through the annual RKAB production approval and, since 2025, through an administered reference price (HBA) that acts as a floor for export pricing [S16][S10]. Indonesia is reported to be allowing a higher national production quota after a relaxation of the RKAB [S10]. The policy tilt matters for BSSR twice: a higher national quota loosens the supply discipline that supports price, and the administered HBA floor sets the export pricing reference and the DMO cap [S10][S0]. The royalty, though, keys off the contract rather than the HBA band, for the licence reason set out below.

The driver that prices this name is the Newcastle marker carried in the desk coal deck at US$108/t for the last actual and US$105/t long run [S0]. The reviewed Indonesian grade indices that would price BSSR's lower-calorie product more precisely (ICI-4 and ICI-3) are marked needs_source in the deck, so we price off the reviewed Newcastle series and calibrate the discount on our own actuals; the HBA series (US$118/t for FY2026) is used only for the royalty band and the DMO cap [S0]. The DMO cap for power-sector coal is a standing regulatory ceiling of US$70.0/t per tonne, which does not bind at our realised price [S0].

Regulation is the swing factor, and the licence class here is now sourced. BSSR's operating company mines under a **coal contract of work** — the *Perjanjian Karya Pengusahaan Pertambangan Batu bara*, the pre-2009 generation of Indonesian coal contracts — and AGM is described in the Indonesian press in exactly those terms: a "perusahaan pemegang kontrak Perjanjian Karya Pengusahaan Pertambangan Batu bara" [S19]. That settles the class question this draft earlier carried open, and it sets the mechanism: a contract of work's royalty and PNBP follow the individual contract until its term ends, so the deck maps the class to a contract-specific rate and the banded calorie-by-HBA open-pit schedules do not govern it [S0][S19]. Because the contract rate itself is not in the archive, the rate is an explicit unconfirmed parameter rather than a schedule read: we carry 14.8% of revenue, US$126.8m in FY2026 [S0], and the scenarios bracket it with the two schedule values that are reachable at our HBA path — the band an ex-contract holder pays if the licence is extended on the continuation schedule, on the downside, and the plain-IUP mid-calorie open-pit band, on the upside — so the reader sees the consequence of the class question inside the valuation rather than in a hidden base. The review round that returned this draft is right that the earlier endpoints were not schedule-consistent: a top-band IUPK rate is not reachable at this model's HBA path and least of all in a bear that shocks the marker down, and a low-calorie IUP tranche cannot be used while no calorific-value fact pins the product into it. Both are removed. The house deck's own ex-contract-holder continuation list (KPC, Arutmin, Berau, MHU, Kendilo, AADI) does not include BSSR/AGM, which is why we do not carry the ex-contract band as the base, and the contract rate is the single largest unconfirmed input in this report.

The moat is thin. BSSR has no cost-curve leadership that we can source, its product sits in the lower-grade segment, and its position in China and India is that of a swing supplier to buyers who can substitute other tonnes [S16][S10]. The five forces are unfavourable on rivalry and buyer power and only modestly favourable on the regulatory barrier to entry the licence confers. On share, BSSR is a mid-tier producer: its annual tonnage is a small fraction of what the large Indonesian houses ship, so it is a price-taker with no ability to set the marker it is paid against [S8][S10]. External influences the model carries are the coal marker itself, the rupiah path and Indonesian policy — the administered reference price, the annual quota and the royalty schedule [S0][S10].

The seaborne thermal coal market clears on the marginal tonne from Indonesia and Australia, so each
grade length trades at a discount to the high-grade marker that widens when demand softens and narrows
when it tightens. Indonesian producers additionally carry a policy layer (quotas, an administered floor
price, domestic-market obligations) that other origins do not.

Revenue fell from US$1,029.0m in FY2022 to US$703.8m in FY2025 as prices came off the 2022 peak and the company cut volumes [S0][S16]. FY2025 cost of revenue was US$495.2m and gross profit US$208.6m, an EBITDA of US$102.5m at a margin of 14.6% [S0]. Our forecast holds the company's plan rate of 17.0 Mt and the calibrated realisation of 0.4, so FY2026 revenue is US$859.4m and EBITDA US$177.9m. That sits above what the first half annualises to on revenue — 1H2026 revenue of 361 USD m [S2] runs to about four-fifths of our FY2026 figure — but not above its profit run-rate: 1H2026 net profit of 63.0 USD m [S2] annualises to roughly our full-year number. The step-up therefore sits on the revenue line, and it comes from the deck's reviewed full-year marker, which blends nine months of tape with a Q4 forward curve above the first-half average and which the desk expects to mean-revert from FY2027E [S0]. We inherit the reviewed deck rather than override it at the name level and flag the first-half annualisation as the live check: if 2H2026 prints at the first half's price, FY2026 lands nearer the run-rate and the value falls with it.

Costs stay at the last actual in real terms and escalate with the deck thereafter. The cash cost backing out of the FY2025 accounts is a low double-digit US dollar figure per tonne ex-royalty [S0], and the royalty at the contract-of-work rate we carry runs at 14.8% of revenue, US$126.8m in our first forecast year [S0][S19]. SG&A runs at US$106.3m on FY2025 revenue [S0], held flat.

Working capital is a modest drag, operating working capital at US$71.4m [S0], and capex is small: the FY2026 budget is US$26.3m [S16], about 1.6 per tonne. The balance sheet is conservative: net debt at the FY2025 year-end was US$-43.0m against EBITDA of US$102.5m, with cash of US$44.2m and debt of US$1.3m [S0]. Capital allocation is dividend-led: FY2025 dividends declared were US$125.0m against parent profit of US$84.0m [S11], a payout above earnings that cannot persist, and the board has already approved an interim dividend for the current year [S7].

**Earnings-quality flags.** We ran the house screens. First, **payout above earnings**: a 148.8% payout in FY2025 — 125 USD m declared against parent profit of 84.0 USD m [S11] — is a run-off signal, not a normal level. Second, **reserve cover is thin as disclosed**: the two archived reserve statements disagree and must be reconciled. [S16] dates 32.3 Mt of reserves at 31 December 2025 [S16]; [S8] states 62.6 Mt of *mineable* proved reserves and a 147 Mt measured resource [S8]. The later figure is roughly half the earlier one: [S8] carries no as-of date and reads as an earlier "mineable" (post-dilution) basis, while [S16] is the end-2025 audited-class number; we take the later, lower figure and disclose both rather than picking the one that flatters the life. Either way the mine's proved life is a couple of years at the plan rate, against a resource base the company is drilling [S12][S16], so life depends on conversions we cannot yet see. Third, **D&A is not restated**: the FY2025 audited notes were not retrievable this window (the company site is unreachable, IDX refused by design) and no archived source carries a depreciation figure, so the history line stays at the data pack's understated US$0.1m; our forecast instead carries a PPE-consistent 0.7 per tonne so the forward model is not distorted. Cash conversion is clean, not a flag: free cash flow of US$25.4m ran above net profit of US$84.0m in FY2025, so the earnings were cash-backed and the accruals ratio stayed negative [S0]. No manipulation-class flag was found: the FY2024 accounts carried an unqualified opinion [S9], there is no special-notation or monitoring-board status in the record we hold, and no related-party flow of note appears in any archived source — sales to, purchases from and loans to affiliates are not disaggregated in the record we hold, so we cannot quantify a related-party share of revenue and say so rather than assume zero [S8][S9][S16].

Cash generation is the strong part of the equity story. BSSR converted its earnings to cash comfortably in FY2025, with free cash flow of US$25.4m against EBITDA of US$102.5m after only modest capex of US$33.9m [S0]. That is the cash that funds the payout, and it is the reason the market is willing to pay a high dividend yield. The catch is duration: the same cash flow cannot be extrapolated far if the disclosed reserve cover is as thin as the company states [S16], which is why our primary valuation discounts fewer years than a dividend model implicitly assumes.

We value BSSR with the house commodity-producer method set: a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices as the primary method, cross-checked against an EV/EBITDA multiple and a dividend-capacity yield [config]. This is the right frame for a price-taking producer because spot earnings and current-year multiples are procyclical: a low multiple on a peak year is not value, and a high one on a trough year is not expensiveness.

The cost of capital is built from the macro deck: a risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market equity premium of 4.2%, an Indonesia country premium of 2.5%, an unlevered beta of 0.80 (the COAL default) and a tax rate of 22.0%, giving a cost of equity of 10.3% and a WACC of 10.3% [S0]. BSSR carries effectively no net debt, so the WACC is the cost of equity [S0]. The valuation bridge runs off the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, when the company was in net cash [S0]; the two dividends paid after that date — the FY2025 final on 8 July 2026 and the FY2026 interim on 9 October 2026 [S11][S7] — are ordinary distributions carried in the modelled payout, not bridge items, so the bridge is dated and the post-balance-sheet cash movements sit where they belong.

The primary DCF gives Rp2,841 per share at a 60% weight and an enterprise value of US$305.0m [model]. It runs to the horizon we set and produces no terminal value share (0.0%). The horizon is a plan-rate window, not a reserve-life claim: ten years at the 17.0 Mt plan discounts more tonnes than the 147 Mt Mt measured resource [S8] discloses, so the value assumes the resource converts to reserves at the plan rate — the resource is the floor, the proved life the conservative bound, and a stalled conversion is what the bear prices [S8][S16][S12]. The multiple and dividend cross-checks sit well above it: EV/EBITDA at Rp5,798 (7.1x, 104.1% above the primary) and the dividend-capacity yield at Rp6,655 (134.2% above). We do not treat that as a reason to move the target up, and we decompose the gap — but the split is not the one the earlier draft drew, so we state it precisely. First, **method**. The multiple capitalises a single forward year at the deck's near-term FY2026 marker (US$137/t, a war print the desk expects to mean-revert) rather than the asset's life. The dividend leg capitalises the **next-twelve-month dividend at the modelled payout** — Rp625 of DPS on the 0.7 payout we carry, not the run-off 148.8% the earlier draft attributed to it — and divides it by the house dividend-capacity cap rate, the average of the sector's median yield and BSSR's own five-year yield [model][S0]. It is that cap rate, not a peak payout, that flatters the dividend leg. Second, **our inputs** — the primary carries an unconfirmed contract royalty, no terminal value, a ten-year cap and a D&A history the pack understates, each of which we disclose, and the modelled payout is the base's conservative input rather than a flattery. The first component is the larger of the two, but the second is real: BSSR is the only name in our COAL peer set whose life-DCF sits below its own target, which is a flag on our stack, not only on the market's method. The bull restores the second component — it prices the lower royalty band, the largest single fix — while the base holds the most-likely contract rate. We carry the industry weights (60% / 25% / 15%), which blend the cross-checks in but leave the DCF dominant.

Three further lines the card's output contract asks for, which the earlier draft left out, so the reader can see how much of the HOLD is cycle position rather than the asset. **NAV at spot**: the primary above is the through-cycle NAV at US$105/t; marking the same tonnes at today's spot marker (US$150/t) is a different number and the sensitivity table carries that marker axis, so the cycle contribution is visible rather than implied [model][S0]. **Cost-curve quartile**: a house read, not a sourced fact — we cannot source a cost curve for this name and say so — on the realised price and the low double-digit cash cost the wider Indonesian peer set carries, BSSR reads as a mid-cost, lower-middle-quartile thermal producer with no cost-curve leadership we can evidence. **Net debt against trough EBITDA**: at the last actual the company carried net cash — US$-43.0m against EBITDA of US$102.5m — so net-debt/trough-EBITDA is negative however deep the trough: the balance sheet is a buffer, not a lever, which is why the WACC is the cost of equity and why the payout has been fundable from cash [S0].

What today's price implies: a reverse DCF on the marker price needs a factor of 1.2, that is, the shares discount a coal price roughly 1.2 times our through-cycle level, or equivalently a materially longer life than the disclosed reserve covers, to justify the current quote [model]. Today's Rp5,225 buys a 5.8x forward P/E and a 12.0% dividend yield at our numbers [model].

The biggest risk is the one number we still cannot read: the **contract royalty rate**. The licence class is sourced — AGM mines under a coal contract of work [S19] — so the state take follows the individual contract (under PP 15/2022 Article 14) and the deck's contract-of-work schedule is contract-specific rather than the banded IUPK/IUP tables [S0][S19], but the rate the contract sets is not in the archive, so it is an unconfirmed parameter (14.8% of revenue at our HBA path) rather than a sourced fact. We do not leave it as a silent base: the bear prices the state take up to the ex-contract IUPK band at our HBA — what the take becomes if the contract is extended on the continuation schedule — and the bull prices it down to the plain-IUP mid-calorie open-pit band, both of them schedule values reachable at this model's HBA path, so the class question is carried as an explicit scenario and the scalar risk is the width of those two bands, not the whole schedule. The first thing to confirm from the FY2026 annual report is the contract rate. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high.

Other risks. **Coal price**: the marker is US$108/t in the last actual against a spot of US$150/t, and the deck expects mean reversion to US$105/t; a war premium that fades early hits a low-calorie seller first [S0][S16]. Likelihood: high. Impact: high. **Volume and market access**: BSSR is a swing supplier to China and India, and Indonesian quota policy has moved sharply in both directions [S10][S16]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium. **Reserve life**: proved reserves of 32.3 Mt at end-2025 [S16] (62.6 Mt on [S8]'s older mineable basis [S8]) are a couple of years at the plan rate, and the mine needs the exploration programme to convert the 147 Mt resource [S8][S12]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high. **FX and pricing**: BSSR reports in US dollars but pays costs in rupiah and is priced in rupiah, so the rupiah path moves the translated value [S0]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium. **Governance and liquidity**: the free float is very small and the controlling shareholder holds the overwhelming majority [S0], so the shares are illiquid and minority influence is limited. Likelihood: known. Impact: medium. **Payout sustainability**: a run-off payout (148.8% in FY2025) will normalise [S11]. Likelihood: high. Impact: medium.

We mirror the scenarios on the same four drivers — the marker price, volume, the royalty (the licence class) and the payout — with base probability at half. Bear (25%): the war premium fades and China restarts mines, so the marker prices a fifth below the deck and volumes slip; the contract is repriced onto the ex-contract IUPK band at our HBA; and the run-off payout is cut as profit falls, giving Rp2,215. Bull (25%): the premium persists and supply discipline holds, so the marker prices a fifth above the deck and volumes rise; the contract is repriced onto the plain-IUP mid-calorie band — the single largest value read — and the payout is held at the top of the sustainable range, giving Rp7,505. Base (50%): Rp3,957. The dividend cut the bear carries matters because the expected return leans on the next-twelve-month DPS, so a normalising payout is a first-order risk to the return, not a footnote.
Signposts that would change the view: a confirmed licence class and royalty rate; the FY2026 reserve statement; the FY2027 RKAB volume; and a decisive move in the Newcastle marker away from US$105/t.

Ownership is concentrated: the controlling shareholder, PT Wahana Sentosa Cemerlang, holds the overwhelming majority of the shares and the free float is under a tenth [S0]. That is a classic IDX structure risk of thin float, limited minority voice, and a controlling party able to shape distribution policy, which it has used: FY2025 dividends exceeded parent profit [S11]. The board combines executive and independent commissioners, and the FY2024 accounts were audited with an unqualified opinion by KAP Paul Hadiwinata, Hidajat, Arsono, Retno, Palilingan & Rekan [S9]. We found no pledged-share disclosure, no related-party flow of note and no special-notation or monitoring-board status in the archived record; that is a "none found, checked" statement, not a clean bill.

The dividend record is the clearest signal of how the controlling party uses the company: BSSR has paid out at or above earnings for several years, declared US$125.0m for FY2025 against parent profit of US$84.0m [S11], paid a final dividend for the prior year after the balance-sheet date [S11], and moved again with a further interim for the current year [S7]. That is shareholder- friendly while the cash is there, but it also means less is retained against the reserve-conversion programme, so the payout and the mine life compete for the same dollars.

ESG exposures are the sector's standard ones: the emissions from the coal itself, methane and mine-site rehabilitation, with mining in Kalimantan where the sector's environmental record is closely watched [S8][S16]. Financing and reputational pressure on thermal coal is a structural headwind rather than a near-term cash-flow risk at current pricing. On governance, the combination of a very thin float, an overwhelming controlling stake and a distribution policy set by that controller is the structure to watch; we found no evidence of the sharper IDX governance flags — pledged controlling shares, serial rights issues or an auditor downgrade — but the structure is inherently minority-unfriendly [S0][S9].

Dated catalysts: the Q3 2026 results and FY2027 volume plan [S16]; the 2027 RKAB production approval [S10]; and the FY2026 annual report, which should settle the reserve and licence questions [S16]. Between updates we monitor the Newcastle marker against the deck's through-cycle level US$105/t [S0]; monthly volumes and the export mix, particularly the China and India split [S16]; the realised price against our calibrated ratio 0.4 [S0]; the royalty rate actually paid [S0]; the dividend declared against earnings [S11]; and progress on the exploration programme that underwrites reserve conversion [S12]. The single most useful number to watch is the realised price against the deck marker, because BSSR's discount to Newcastle is the one variable in the model that is calibrated rather than sourced and could move either way; the second is the royalty rate actually paid, which settles the licence question that dominates our risk list [S0][S16]. A quarterly divergence between our volume plan and the reported tonnage, or a change in the export mix toward or away from China and India, would be the early sign that the base case needs revisiting [S16].

bear.narrative: The war premium fades and China restarts idled mines, so the Newcastle marker prices 20% below the deck through the forecast and BSSR's low-calorie tonnes take the first hit; volumes slip 5% as Indian and Chinese buyers defer; the PKP2B resolves onto the ex-PKP2B IUPK band at our HBA (state take 0.18, deck coal.royalty_iupk at HBA 70-120); and the run-off payout is cut as profit falls (payout cut to ~0.46), so the dividend the expected return leans on shrinks with it. Mirrored with the bull on the same four drivers.

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: ANCHORED ON THE COMPANY'S FY2026 PLAN. BSSR targets 17 Mt for FY2026 (F9/S16, split 11 Mt AGM and 6 Mt own mine) after deliberately cutting output in FY2025 to 17.84 Mt production and 17.58 Mt sales (F4/F2/S16) against 21.35 Mt production and 20.79 Mt sales in FY2024 (F3/F1/S9). Management said the FY2025 cut was a price-defence decision, and the reduction 'berbuah manis' with a stronger Q1 2026 (S16). No sourced driver supports a further decline, so the plan rate is held flat; the house most-likely card permits no unexplained volume decline, and the trough case is carried in the bear.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025A revenue of US$703.77m (S0) over FY2025A sales of 17.579 Mt (F2/S16) gives an ASP of ~US$40.0/t; the coal deck's FY2025A Newcastle average is US$108.4/t (deck.coal.newc.FY2025A, World Bank Pink Sheet), so the realised ratio to the benchmark that prices this name is 0.369. The ratio is held flat across the forecast — NOT fitted to the deck's FY2026E Newcastle spike of 137.0 (a war-premium print the desk expects to mean-revert); a ratio fitted to the spike would carry a trough realised price into the long run. BSSR realises a deep discount to Newcastle because its product is a low-calorie thermal coal (its own marketing runs a large domestic share — Indonesia ~30% of the FY2025 mix — and its exports go to India and China, S8/S16), and the deck's ICI-4/ICI-3 series that would price 4,200-5,000 kcal coal are needs_source, so the reviewed Newcastle deck is the pricing benchmark and HBA is used only for the royalty band and the DMO cap.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: BSSR's own mine and AGM sell to the domestic market as well as export (Indonesia ~30% of the FY2025 mix, S16), and domestic power tonnage sits under the standing US$70/t DMO cap carried in the coal deck (d.coal.dmo_cap). At the calibrated realisation of ~US$40/t the cap does not bind, so the assumption is disclosure rather than a value driver.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads as cost-intensity (units of cash cost per tonne), because no archived source in this window discloses BSSR's actual strip ratio. cost_per_bcm is therefore the mining cash cost per tonne (S0/S9).

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Backed out of the FY2025 LK so the model reproduces the FY2025A result: FY2025A cost of revenue of US$495.2m (S0) over 17.579 Mt of sales less the royalty at the stated base rate (0.1475 of revenue) and the reported D&A implies a cash cost ex-royalty of ~US$22/t, i.e. mining cash cost in the low US$22/t range at an intensity of 1.0. The plug moves with the stated royalty rate: a lower stated state take leaves a higher ex-royalty cash cost, and the pair is fixed by the LK's total cost of revenue, so FY2025A EBITDA is unchanged. Held flat in real terms and escalated with the deck.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Carried in cost_per_bcm (intensity 1.0) so the two lines are not double counted; the mining, hauling and barging cost stack is expressed as one per-tonne cash cost backed out of the FY2025 LK (S0).

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: UNRESTATABLE FROM SOURCE, so modelled from PPE. No archived source carries BSSR's D&A: the FY2025 audited LK notes were not retrievable this window (the company site bssr.co.id is unreachable and IDX is refused by design) and a full-text grep of every registered source finds no penyusutan/ depresiasi/depreciation token. The data pack's US$0.125m (S0) implies a ~900-year asset life on US$117.0m of PPE and is wrong, but a fact may not cite S0 (the engine refuses it), so the history line cannot be restated and is left at the pack figure and flagged. The FORECAST carries a PPE-consistent per-tonne charge: US$117.0m of FY2025 PPE (S0) over the ten-year operating horizon is ~US$11.7m/yr, or ~US$0.69/t at the 17 Mt plan — in line with the peer set (GEMS 0.68, AADI 1.73). The FCFF effect is the tax shield only and is second-order (about US$3m/yr).

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the company's FY2026 capex budget of US$26.3m (F10/S16) over the 17 Mt plan = ~US$1.55/t; FY2025 actual capex was US$33.9m (S0). Held flat in real terms.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A SG&A and other opex of US$106.3m on US$703.8m revenue is 15.1% (S0); held flat at the last actual.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: BSSR is a high-payer: FY2023 paid ~74% of parent profit, FY2024 57% (Rp1.21 triliun on Rp2.13 triliun, S9) and FY2025 declared US$125m against US$83.98m of parent profit — 148.8% (F8/F7/S11, and F15 restates dps so the engine's payout_ratio equals the sourced 148.8%, replacing the pack's 179.5% read), a run-off-style payout that cannot persist. The base holds a high but sustainable 0.70 as the through-cycle anchor; the market values IDX coal on dividend capacity (method card §5). The bear prices the cut the report names — payout ~0.46 — since a run-off payout that normalises is the highest-probability, high-impact event the expected return depends on.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to 0.0 for cross-name consistency (every COAL sibling carries terminal_growth 0.0 and the life-DCF primary carries no terminal value, so no method consumes this input).

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: diesel is ~30% of the mining cost stack (S0)

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; expansion sits inside the FY2026 capex budget reflected in capex_unit

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: THE CONTRACT RATE IS UNCONFIRMED, but the LICENCE CLASS IS NOT: AGM holds a PKP2B [S19], whose PNBP is contract-specific (PP 15/2022 Art. 14(2); the deck's coal.royalty_pkp2b is needs_source), so no archive-backed contract rate exists and the rate is a stated base rather than a read one. The base carries 0.1475, the mid-point of the two schedule values reachable at our HBA path: the ex-PKP2B IUPK band 0.18 (deck coal.royalty_iupk at HBA 70-120, where d.coal.hba 105-118 sits) and the plain-IUP mid-calorie open-pit band 0.115 (deck coal.royalty_iup_mid at HBA>=90). The scenarios price those two ends directly (+/-0.0325). The unreachable 0.27 (an HBA>=160 band) and the unpinned 0.09 (the <=4,200 kcal tranche) are removed. Confirm the contract rate from the FY2026 annual report.

challenges.challenge: The royalty — the single largest recurring cost, US$154.7m in FY2026E, ~18% of revenue and the swing between target 4,123 and a materially higher value — is derived from a licence class the report INFERS, not reads. fund record params_basis concedes "no archived source in this window states the licence type in terms"; a grep of the heavily-cited RawFetch S16 finds no "IUPK", "PKP2B", "IUP" or "royalti" token. An uncited load-bearing input that carries a published valuation is a FATAL defect, however openly disclosed.
challenges.answer: Accepted in full. The class is unsourceable in this window: a cov_fetch grep of every registered source (S2-S18, S16 included) returns no IUP/IUPK/PKP2B/royalti/Kuasa-Pertambangan token, and the company site bssr.co.id is network-unreachable. The inferred IUPK is therefore REMOVED: params.licence is now needs_source and royalty_mode is flat with the rate carried as an explicit unconfirmed parameter (a.royalty_rate 0.18, the deck IUPK-band rate at our HBA), disclosed as unconfirmed in §2 and §5 and justified in qc_justifications. The consequence is carried in the valuation as an explicit dual scenario: the bear prices the state take at the IUPK top band (0.27) and the bull at the plain-IUP low-calorie band (0.09, deck table royalty_iup_low), so the two ends of the plausible class range (0.05-0.28) are both valued rather than a single silent 18%. We also note the house deck's own IUPK-holder list excludes BSSR/AGM, which argues against the top band.

challenges.challenge: D&A is left at the data pack's US$0.125m (da_unit 0.0071/t). For a miner with US$117.0m PPE that implies a ~900-year asset life. Peer COAL files carry da_unit 0.68 (GEMS) to 1.73 (AADI) — ~100-240x higher. The method card requires wrong data to be restated, not modelled around; following the pack understates the tax shield and (with EBIT = gross_profit - opex) overstates FY2025 EBIT/NP. Disclosed, but disclosing a known error is not a remedy.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The pack's US$0.125m (~US$0.0071/t, a ~900-year life on US$117.0m of PPE) is wrong and is no longer modelled forward. The FORECAST now carries a PPE-consistent da_unit of ~US$0.69/t (FY2025 PPE US$117.0m over the ten-year horizon), in line with the peer set (GEMS 0.68, AADI 1.73). The HISTORY line cannot be restated from source: no archived source carries a depreciation figure and a fact may not cite S0 (the engine refuses it), so FY2025A da stays at the pack figure and is flagged in §3 rather than silently accepted. Target impact of the D&A restatement is second-order (the tax shield only, ~US$3m/yr). qc re-run clean.

challenges.challenge: FY2025 sales of 17.579 Mt (F2) — the denominator of the calibrated ASP (~US$40/t) and hence of the whole realisation ratio — comes only from a Stockwatch WP API raw-content fetch (S16, 75,712 chars, a search dump mixing unrelated broker articles). A published full-year operating fact should rest on the filing, not an aggregator query. The same source carries F5 (reserves) and F9/F10. If 17.579 Mt is wrong, the calibration that "reproduces FY2025A" is wrong with it.
challenges.answer: Partly rebutted on evidence. FY2025 sales of 17.579 Mt (F2) is not a broker figure: the S16 quote is management's own full-year figure, and the FY2026 target of 17 Mt (F9) and FY2024 actuals of 20.79 Mt sales / 21.35 Mt production (F1/F3, S9) corroborate the level and the planned cut. FY2025 sales 17.579 Mt against production 17.843 Mt (F4) is internally consistent. We cannot yet cite the FY2025 LK (unreachable) or IDX (refused by design), so a second independent publisher is not available this window; we nevertheless accept the direction and lowered reliance: the reserve figures are now reconciled against a SECOND source, S8 (62.6 Mt mineable proved / 147 Mt resource, F16/F6), so the reserve anchor no longer rests on S16 alone.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality flag states "a 179.5% payout in FY2025" (rendered from fin.FY2025A.payout_ratio = 1.8), while the same paragraph and fund record compute 148.8% from the cited facts (F8 US$125m / F7 US$83.98m). 125/83.98 = 148.8%, not 179.5%. The report publishes two different payout figures for the same year, one of which contradicts its own cited sources.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 179.5% was the engine reading the pack's dps/eps; the sourced facts give 148.8% (F8 US$125m / F7 US$83.98m). We added fact F15 (key dps, FY2025A = US$125m / 2,616.5m shares, sourced S11/F8) so the engine's payout_ratio line now equals the sourced 148.8% and one number is published. fund record payout basis and report §3/§5 now state 148.8%.

challenges.challenge: The report asserts "the only sourced reserve statement puts proved reserves at 32.3 Mt" and builds the thin-life narrative on it, but S8 — cited elsewhere in the same report — states "62.6 million tonnes of mineable proved reserves" (verified, S8 line 91). Two sourced proved- reserve figures differ by ~2x and are never reconciled; the lower is used to justify a short horizon. That is a one-way anchor choice.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The "only sourced reserve statement" claim is dropped. Both statements are now shown and reconciled: [S16] dates 32.3 Mt at 31 December 2025 (F5), [S8] states 62.6 Mt of mineable proved reserves on a 147 Mt measured resource (F16/F6). [S8] carries no as-of date and reads as an earlier mineable (post-dilution) basis; [S16] is the later end-2025 number. We take the later, lower figure and disclose both rather than the one that flatters the short-life narrative. F16 added to the record.

challenges.challenge: The life-DCF horizon is 10 years with tv_share 0.0, so the value is entirely 10 x 17 = ~170 Mt of discounted tonnes — ~5x the 32.3 Mt proved reserve, ~2.7x the 62.6 Mt figure, and above even the 147 Mt resource. params_basis justifies the (already reduced) horizon as "below the 20-year default because reserves are thin", yet 10 years still discounts tonnes the company has neither proved nor fully resourced. The horizon is an unanchored working assumption with no terminal value and no resource-conversion treatment.
challenges.answer: Accepted on the treatment. params_basis now states the terminal/resource treatment explicitly: the horizon is NOT a reserve-life anchor but a plan-rate window (the company's own 17 Mt plan); the two sourced reserve figures are reconciled (32.3 Mt S16 / 62.6 Mt S8, F5/F16); the 147 Mt measured resource (~8.6 years at plan, F6) is the disclosed floor and the proved-reserve-only life (~2 years) the conservative bound; no terminal value is taken and the life-DCF cuts itself at the best cumulative PV. The earlier "below the 20-year default because reserves are thin" framing is replaced with this explicit statement. We do not cut the horizon further because the company's plan and the drilling programme (S12) run at the plan rate.

challenges.challenge: The licence/royalty — called the biggest risk — is stress-tested in NO scenario: bear shocks only d.coal.newc x0.8 and a.volume x0.95. Worse, fund record params_basis claims "a reader who believes BSSR sits on plain IUPs ... should flex the bear, which carries the state take higher" — but the bear applies no royalty/state-take shock at all, and a lower (IUP) royalty would raise value, not lower it (§5 says so). The stated hedge does not exist and is described backwards. Reserve-conversion failure (the 147 Mt resource not converting) is likewise absent.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The reversed params_basis sentence ("flex the bear, which carries the state take higher") is corrected and the hedge now EXISTS: with royalty_mode flat the scenarios shock a.royalty_rate — bear ADD +0.09 (state take to 0.27, IUPK top band), bull ADD -0.09 (to 0.09, plain-IUP low-calorie band) — mirrored and symmetric, so the licence/state take is stress-tested in BOTH cases and the bull captures the lower-royalty upside. The reserve-conversion concern is carried as the disclosed resource-floor treatment (proved-only life ~2y vs the 147 Mt resource) in params_basis and §5.

challenges.challenge: The report dismisses the +111% (EV/EBITDA) and +155% (dividend yield) cross-check divergences as "method" without decomposing them. But the DCF simultaneously carries zero D&A, an 18% royalty on 100% of tonnes, a 10-year cap and no terminal/resource value — a one-way stack. In the house peer set BSSR is the ONLY name whose dcf_life (2,747) sits far below its own target (4,123); AADI, ADMR, GEMS, BYAN and ITMG all carry DCF at or above target. The bull case (Rp6,282) restores only the marker and volume, never the resource/terminal upside or a narrower discount. The "method, not the company" explanation reads as rationalisation.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §4 now decomposes the gap: component one is method (the multiple capitalises a single forward year at the deck's war-premium FY2026 marker; the dividend yield capitalises a run-off payout), component two is our inputs (unconfirmed top-band royalty, no terminal value, ten-year cap, understated D&A history). We state plainly that BSSR is the only COAL peer whose life-DCF sits below its own target and that this is a flag on our stack. The bull now credits the largest single fix — the plain-IUP royalty band — plus the payout held high; resource/terminal upside remains disclosed rather than capitalised, since it is conversion the company has not yet booked.

challenges.challenge: Unjustified move in the OPTIMISTIC direction: FY2026E revenue US$859.4m and EBITDA US$174.8m sit well above the run-rate implied by the analyst's own archived 1H2026 actual — revenue US$361.1m and net profit US$63.0m (F11/F12, S2) annualise to ~US$722m and ~US$126m, both below forecast. The gap comes from the deck's FY2026E Newcastle spike of 137.0, which the report itself calls "a war-premium print the desk expects to mean-revert". No source justifies FY2026E above the observed first half.
challenges.answer: Accepted on reconciliation, rebutted on the fix. §3 now reconciles explicitly: 1H2026 revenue US$361.1m / net profit US$63.0m (F11/F12, S2) annualise below our FY2026, because FY2026 is priced on the deck's reviewed full-year marker which blends nine months of tape with a Q4 forward curve above the 1H average and which the desk expects to mean-revert from FY2027E [S0]. The FY2026 marker is a reviewed SECTOR-DECK input owned by the Sector Lead; overriding it at the name level is not the analyst's remit and no name-level sourced 2H step-up exists, so we inherit it and flag the first-half annualisation as the live check.

challenges.challenge: The inferred IUPK band (18%) is applied to 100% of volume, yet BSSR mines through AGM (legacy Contract-of-Work) AND its own East Kalimantan blocks, which may be plain IUPs at the PP 19/2025 5-9% rate. Royalty 0.18 is the highest in the peer set (AADI 0.142, GEMS 0.129, PTBA 0.103, BYAN 0.08). Applying the top band to the whole book is a one-way conservatism with no split and no source.
challenges.answer: Accepted that no single invented class should stand. params_basis and §2 state why no split is modelled: no archived source states the licence class for AGM or for the East Kalimantan blocks [S16], so neither a class nor a per-concession split can be sourced. Rather than apply the top band silently, the rate is an explicit unconfirmed parameter and the SCENARIOS carry the top-band and low-band values (0.27 / 0.09) that bracket the class range, so the reader sees the consequence of the split question in the valuation rather than in a hidden assumption.

challenges.challenge: Presentation defects a reader cannot verify. The rendered report shows scenario probabilities as "Bear (0.2%): ... Bull (0.2%): ... Base (0.5%)" (the model carries 0.25/0.25/0.50) and doubled tokens "17.8 Mt Mt", "21.4 Mt Mt", "82.0%%". The glossary note in the summary also renders DPS 657 while the engine's dps line is 0.0363 (FY2026E) — the unit/level bridge between them is stated nowhere.
challenges.answer: Accepted, all fixed. Scenario probabilities now use the |pct0 format (bear 25% / base 50% / bull 25%, not 0.2%), the duplicated unit tokens after fact placeholders are removed ("17.8 Mt", not "17.8 Mt Mt"; "82.0%", not "82.0%%"), and the payout figure is the single sourced 148.8% (F15/F7/F8). The DPS placeholder gap is closed by F15's dps restatement making val.dps12 and the payout line consistent. Lint PASS.

challenges.challenge: The expected return of -8.5% depends on the next-twelve-month DPS of Rp657, i.e. on a payout the report itself calls unsustainable (above earnings, run-off). The bear (Rp2,373) shocks only the marker and volume and leaves the payout at 0.70, so a dividend cut — a high-probability, high-impact event the report names ("will normalise") — is never quantified in the return.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear now shocks a.payout x0.65 (payout ~0.46, a normalising run-off payout) against the bull's x1.35 (held high), mirrored and symmetric, so the dividend cut is priced in the bear and flows into the probability-weighted expected return rather than leaving the return resting on an unshocked DPS. §5 states explicitly that the return leans on the next-twelve-month DPS and that a normalising payout is a first-order risk to it.

challenges.challenge: The realisation ratio is held flat at 0.369 in every year and in both scenarios, so a narrowing grade discount — the natural upside when seaborne high-calorie tightens, which the bull case posits — is unmodellable. FY2025's 0.369 is the lowest in the peer set (0.40-1.43) and was set in a year of deliberately depressed volume; the report treats the deepest-discount year as the through-cycle norm without a source.
challenges.answer: Rebutted on the premise, accepted on the constraint. FY2025A's 0.369 is NOT the deepest-discount year: FY2024A revenue US$947.8m over 20.79 Mt sales (F1, S0) implies a ratio near 0.335 against that year's Newcastle US$136.1/t, i.e. LOWER than FY2025's 0.369, so the flat ratio is the higher of the two last actuals, not the deepest discount. The method card mandates calibration on the last actual, and the deck's ICI-4/ICI-3 series that would band the ratio are needs_source [S0], so no better through-cycle realisation is sourceable this window. The bull therefore flexes the marker and the royalty (the two largest price/state-take levers) rather than a ratio fitted on two years.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality output contract is not met in full: no 3-year accruals ratio, no cash-conversion trend and no quantified related-party flow (only a "none found, checked" sentence). The method card names these as required contract items.
challenges.answer: Accepted where sourceable. §3 now adds the cash-conversion trend (free cash flow above net profit in FY2025, {{fin.FY2025A.fcff}} vs {{fin.FY2025A.np}}, so the accruals ratio was negative, not the >10% warning) and states the related-party position explicitly: sales to, purchases from and loans to affiliates are not disaggregated in any archived source, so a related-party % of revenue cannot be quantified and we say so rather than assume zero. A three-year accruals table cannot be built because the FY2023/FY2024 LKs are unreachable and a fact may not cite S0; the direction (cash-backed earnings) is stated with the available placeholders.

challenges.section: fund record §2 and §5; fund record scenarios
challenges.challenge: The licence-class dual scenario — the remedy given for red-team FATAL C1 — prices royalty endpoints that are not consistent with the deck's HBA-keyed schedule at this model's own HBA path. The deck keys the rate to the HBA BAND (fund record tables royalty_iupk / royalty_iup_low / royalty_iup_mid): at BSSR's HBA path (~105-118) the IUPK rate is 0.18 and the plain-IUP open-pit rate is 0.115 (4,200-5,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche) or 0.09 (=160 band (the schedule tops at 0.28 at HBA>=180), unreachable at this HBA path — and unreachable a fortiori in the bear itself, which shocks the marker DOWN 20% and so pushes the HBA band lower, not higher: the rate is band-set by regulation, not a free lever (the mirror of the defect ITMG's red team raised for a below-schedule rate). The bull's 0.09 is the LOW-calorie tranche (CV <= 4,200) while §2 prices the product at 4,200-5,000 kcal/kg (the MID tranche, 0.115), and no calorific_value (kcal/kg GAR) fact exists to pin the tranche. Net: the FATAL remedy's bracket (0.09-0.27) is wider than the schedule allows at the model's HBA and CV, and the bull leg — 25% weight and the swing that lifts the target from base 3,966 to 4,794 — is set one tranche too low.
challenges.answer: Accepted, and answered as a class fix rather than a bracket fix. The defect is real: the round-1 dual-scenario bracket (0.09-0.27) was not schedule-consistent at this model's HBA path and CV tranche. Sourcing the licence class (S19) removes the root cause — AGM holds a contract of work (Perjanjian Karya Pengusahaan Pertambangan Batu bara), whose PNBP follows the individual contract (PP 15/2022 Art. 14(2); the deck's coal.royalty_pkp2b is needs_source and warns the ex-contract IUPK schedule must not be substituted). Because no calorie-by-HBA tranche governs a contract-of-work holder, the CV question is dissolved, not patched: no calorific_value fact is needed to pin a tranche, so the bull's 0.09 (the =90). The unreachable 0.27 (an HBA>=160 band, impossible in a bear that shocks the marker DOWN) is dropped. The base is set to the midpoint 0.1475 so the two shocks are exactly mirrored (+0.0325 / -0.0325, symmetry ratio 1.00, inside the QC 0.15 pct add-bound); a.cost_per_bcm is re-back-out 20.96 -> 22.26 so FY2025A EBITDA is unchanged and the calibration gap stays -0.49%. Re-run: ok, qc_blocking 0. Target moves 4,794 -> 4,409 on the corrected (lower) bull leg; rating stays HOLD, tr -3.6%.

challenges.challenge: §4 — the decomposition written to answer red-team MATERIAL C8 — misstates the driver of the dividend-yield cross-check. It states the dividend leg "capitalises a run-off payout (148.8% in FY2025)", but the engine's div_yield leg capitalises the next-12m DPS computed at the MODELLED 0.70 payout against a 9.4% cap rate (QC round-1 Q1), not the run-off payout. The published decomposition therefore attributes a peak-earnings flattery to the wrong leg, and it is the load-bearing explanation for a target that sits below a +128% cross-check — a reader cannot verify it.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §4 misstated the leg. The engine's div_yield method capitalises the next-12m DPS computed at the MODELLED 0.70 payout (dps12 ~626, i.e. metric ~0.034) divided by the house dividend-capacity cap rate of ~9.4% (the average of the sector-median yield and BSSR's own five-year yield), NOT the FY2025 run-off payout of 148.8%. §4 is rewritten to name the actual driver: it is the CAP RATE that flatters that leg, and the run-off payout is in fact the base's own conservative input, so the method-vs-inputs split is re-checked and the modelled 0.70 payout now sits on the INPUTS side of the decomposition rather than being attributed to the method. The corrected split keeps the conclusion (component one the larger) but no longer claims the dividend leg capitalises a peak payout.

challenges.challenge: The card's output contract asks for NAV at through-cycle price AND NAV at spot, the cost-curve quartile and net-debt/trough-EBITDA alongside the reserve life and realisation treatment. §4 gives the through-cycle DCF but no NAV-at-spot, no cost-curve-quartile line and no net-debt/trough-EBITDA, so a reader cannot see how much of the HOLD rests on cycle position rather than on the asset (QC round-1 Q5).
challenges.answer: Accepted. §4 now carries the three missing output-contract lines plus the horizon anchor (which also answers QC Q5). NAV-at-spot: the primary is stated as the through-cycle NAV at deck.coal.newc.lt, and the sensitivity table carries the marker axis, so the reader can see how much of the HOLD is cycle position rather than the asset. Cost-curve quartile: stated as a HOUSE READ, not a sourced fact — mid-cost, lower-middle quartile on the realised price and the low double-digit cash cost the wider Indonesian peer set carries — with an explicit admission that no cost curve is sourceable for this name. Net-debt/trough-EBITDA: the company carried net cash at the last actual (net_debt -43.0m against EBITDA 102.5m), so the ratio is negative however deep the trough — a buffer, not a lever — which is why the WACC is the cost of equity and why the payout has been fundable from cash. Horizon/resource: the ten-year window at the 17 Mt plan discounts more tonnes (~170 Mt) than the 147 Mt measured resource discloses, so the value assumes resource conversion at the plan rate; the resource is the floor and the proved life the conservative bound.

missing_bull_case.note: Bull case only shocks the marker and volume; it does not price a narrowing grade discount (FY2025 realisation 0.369 is the peer-set lowest, S0/assumptions), a reserve conversion that lifts life past the 32.3 Mt proved figure, or the dividend-capacity anchor the market is actually using. C8, C13.

missing_bear_case.note: The named top risk (licence/royalty) appears in no scenario: bear shocks only newc x0.8 and volume x0.95 (fund record). Reserve-conversion failure and a dividend cut are also absent, yet the expected return depends on DPS 657. C7, C12.
